text:
maria.chen: Heads-up — since we flipped MIG + 4-way time-slice on the eu-west-1 p4d pool, we've seen ~15% more pod evictions and a few long scheduling delays (10-20s). noticed it after the weekend deploy. anyone else?

kevin.s: saw that too. pods with GPU requests >=1 are getting scheduled into the 1-GPU MIG slices and CA can't scale fast enough. cluster-autoscaler log shows a rate limit on creates.

samir: is the CA scaling policy using the zonal balancing flag? if MIG creates smaller allocatable capacity per node, CA's binpacking heuristics get weird.

maria.chen: CA is running with --balance-similar-node-groups=true and scale-down disabled for edge pools. we do allow cross-zone balancing for that cluster.

kevin.s: can you paste the nodepool config? curious about max surge / max size.

maria.chen: here's the nodepool snippet we used for eu-west-1 p4d:

```yaml
- name: p4d-shared-mig-4way
  minSize: 2
  maxSize: 18
  instanceType: p4d.24xlarge
  gpuSharing: MIG_4WAY
  taints:
    - key: "gpu-only"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
```

tia: also worth noting we changed the kubelet eviction thresholds to be a bit tighter on mem/kmem recently — might be interacting.

samir: two angles: CA sees fragmentation because each MIG slice reports fractional GPU allocatables. if our pod GPU request granularity doesn't match slice size, scheduler will pack poorly. second, provisioning latency for p4d in eu-west-1 has spiked — cloud API is slower so scale-up time is longer.

maria.chen: suggested quick mitigation: roll back time-slice to 2-way for the busiest zones, or add an intermediary node pool of dedicated full-GPU nodes for large-batch jobs.

kevin.s: can we also increase CA's --max-node-provision-time? currently 15m, maybe bump to 25m to avoid premature eviction decisions while scale-up finishes.

tia: bumping max provision time helps but increases tail latency for cluster reclamation. we should be surgical: only change for that nodepool via autoscaler config annotation.

infra-ops: FYI the cost impact if we flip back to 2-way: our per-token inference cost rises ~9% in eu-west due to lower packing efficiency, estimated from last week's telemetry.

maria.chen: understood. prioritize reliability > cost for customer-facing routes. but for experimental/backfill workloads we can tilt cost first.

samir: propose a step plan: 1) create an intermediary nodepool `p4d-dedicated-large` (min 2/max 6, no MIG) and label for batch jobs; 2) change p4d-shared-mig-4way maxSize +=4 to give CA room; 3) for eu-west AZ-a, switch to MIG_2WAY as canary; 4) increase --max-node-provision-time for that cluster to 25m.

kevin.s: +1. add also `--expander=least-waste` on CA to prefer nodes that reduce fragmentation. it helped on staging.

tia: add a kube-scheduler config tweak to prefer nodes with free GPU capacity when tolerations match; will open a PR.

maria.chen: action items: @kevin.s create the dedicated nodepool terraform PR, @tia scheduler PR, @samir change CA flags, infra-ops to run cost projection. i'll flip MIG_2WAY on AZ-a tonight as a canary (low traffic window).

infra-ops: running cost projection now, will post numbers in this thread.

sre-bot: Incident bot detected increased pod evictions for cluster `prod-eu-1` between 2028-06-12T03:40Z and 2028-06-12T06:00Z. Alert: S3.

kevin.s: thanks — let's reconvene tomorrow after the canary and cost estimates. if evictions persist, we'll fallback fully to dedicated nodes for critical routes. :thumbsup:

maria.chen: noted. tagging @eng-infra. closing loop later with PR links and telemetry. thanks everyone.
